# Policymaker #720: iteration 0159

No Owner request is necessary. I ordered no policy task, and the Shaper keeps ordinary work.

I read records 0156-0158 and the reports of Sessions #710, #712, #713, #714, #716, #717 and #718. All three iterations closed. Iteration 0158 is accepted and improved, and no_progress is 0.

- **Matched comparison 0155:** review #710 and review #714 were NOT-CLEAR. Corrections #713 and #717 merged. Fix #717 changed `/validation_rules/M09`, because the json has no `/rules` key.
- **Review #718 is blocked.** Read, Grep and Bash returned "No such tool available" ([report](.session/history/sessions/718/1511408e4b1ca068b568771cafef828c6c52aaa6a03e6915db0654e8d9f8af53.md)). It did no check, so the closure of finding F-N1 is not verified. The next Shaper must run the same narrow re-check again, with the pointer `/validation_rules/M09`.
- **My check of the #708 routing change failed.** `reviewer` routes to Codex first, but reviewers #710, #714 and #718 all ran on claude-sonnet-5-5 (see each `task.md`). The records give no fallback reason. Review #714 had parked_s 307, which can show a Codex cooldown. The config looks correct (`.github/loop/session_start.py:70`). I made no new routing change, because I have no provider-state evidence.
- **Effect:** the authors and reviewers of the 0155 contract all used the same model family. This is a limitation of these reviews.

I changed only `policy/working-memory.md`. Benchmark readiness, whole-method review and Owner acceptance are still missing. Product quality is not measured.

## Discoveries

- One reviewer Session started without its role tools, so a correct profile does not always give the tools ([#718 task](.session/history/sessions/718/task.md)).

## What next

- The Shaper runs the narrow M09 re-check again. Do not order a new fix for F-N1 before that verdict.
- The next Policymaker checks which model ran the reviewer Sessions. If Codex is still never used, find the cause through provider state, not through another routing edit.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
